chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Jamil from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding the false witness,
He said: 'If the item is still in existence, it is returned to its owner; and if it is not in existence, he is liable for the value of what was destroyed from the man's wealth.'
ai.seo_question: What is the compensation for a false witness if the claimed property is lost?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of *daman* (guarantee) for false witnesses, distinguishing between the return of the specific asset (*in kind*) if it remains intact and monetary compensation (*qiymah*) if it is lost. This ruling underscores the financial liability of the witness for the actual damage caused to the plaintiff, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on precise restitution in civil disputes. It serves as a foundational text for understanding the evidentiary weight and consequences of perjury in Islamic jurisprudence.
